First release of **xvideo**, a command line tool that downloads the videos of **public** X (Twitter) posts.

```bash
xvideo "https://x.com/USERNAME/status/POST_ID"
```

## Features

- Downloads the video of a post, or every video of a multi-video post
- Several URLs per run, or a URL file (`--file`, `-` for stdin). A failing URL never stops the batch
- Quality selection: `--quality best|worst|1080p|720p|…`. Falls back to the best lower quality
- Safe, portable file names (`USERNAME_POSTID.mp4`) with no collisions (`_1`, `_2`…), plus `--overwrite` and `--skip-existing`
- `--metadata`: embeds author, post ID, URL, date, text, resolution and duration without re-encoding
- Progress bar, `--quiet`, `--verbose` (stack traces only in this mode) and `--json` (JSON Lines with a stable `error_type`)
- Configurable `--timeout`, retries with backoff, resumable downloads
- Plain-language error messages: invalid URL, missing post, no video, private content, network, timeout, HTTP, ffmpeg missing, disk full, permission denied…

ffmpeg is optional. It is only used to merge separate audio and video streams, and for `--metadata`.

Only publicly accessible content is supported: no cookies, no credentials, and no way around access restrictions.

## Installation

```bash
pip install https://github.com/stefan-cambodia/xvideo/releases/download/v1.0.0/xvideo-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl
# or
pipx install git+https://github.com/stefan-cambodia/xvideo.git@v1.0.0
```

Requires Python 3.11 or later. Tested on Linux, macOS and Windows with Python 3.11 to 3.14.

SHA-256 checksums of the attached packages are in `SHA256SUMS`.
